element: Public Agencies sector note (one note per competency)
rationale: Merges federal, state, local and Tribal employers. Of 222 notes, 13 match a state term and 10 a local term; 167 name no level of government. Agrees with CA audit section 7: replace with sector-actor role variants and enactment notes.

All six are federal (NEPA timeline, CatEx, One Federal Decision, etc.). State drivers are absent: state environmental policy act amendments, delegation or assumption changes (e.g. Section 404), skills-based hiring orders, federal grant cuts to state programs. Replace with dated, jurisdiction-tagged driver events.

Defined from the proponent side ('securing regulatory authorization for management activities'). State and local permit writers, inspectors and enforcers are the other side of S3 and have no stage for compliance assurance and enforcement. Add regulator-side functions (authorize, inspect, enforce) to the work-function facet.

Do not fit continuous public service operations (water and wastewater plants, environmental health inspection programs, air monitoring networks). Add 'operate' and 'oversee delegated programs' functions. Agrees with CA audit section 8.
Split into (a) regulatory inspection by the authority (SL-C03) and (b) compliance management inside a regulated entity (PS lane). The task bundles and authority differ.
Rewrite as two role-variant enactments: permit writer (regulator, SL-C02) vs permit preparer (applicant/consultant).
Generalize to environmental review under federal, state and Tribal environmental review acts (SL-C08); keep NEPA as an enactment. States staff MEPA and CEQA units.
Keep and deepen: add the case arc from referral to settlement or litigation and expert testimony (SL-C04).
One competency covers monitoring, SIPs, permitting and enforcement. Split at least monitoring/testing (SL-C13) from planning and permitting; route to an air module.
One of few v1 competencies native to local government (MS4). Carry as the seed of a water-utility module.
Valid for state supervisors. Add labor-agreement administration and grievance indicators (MN PCS Principal spec).
Add intergovernmental instruments (cooperative agreements, Good Neighbor agreements, IPA assignments, delegation agreements, grant work plans).
Reframes a hierarchy as coordination. Add program oversight and delegation tasks (SL-C01, SL-C11).
Valid across state and local; link to the mobility instruments in mobility_map.csv.

element: Missing: water/wastewater operations; environmental public health services; solid waste facility regulation; oil and gas regulation; remediation fund administration; environmental financial assistance
rationale: Zero v1 text mentions these functions, yet the sampled state and local classes are full of them (TX Sanitarian, MI lead and copper, PA oil and gas, FL solid waste, MI MUSTA). Add as modules or core competencies (SL-C05 to C15). Agrees with CA audit section 6.

element: F13 Environmental Health & Justice to SOC 29-9021
rationale: 29-9021 is Health Information Technologists, a poor fit. Environmental health specialists are usually coded with environmental scientists and specialists, including health (19-2041), with SOC 2018 to be verified by FH/IA. State Sanitarian classes are a separate crosswalk target.
25-4031 is Library Technicians, a poor fit. FH/IA to propose a replacement; at state level interpretive and education roles sit in park ranger and naturalist classes (e.g. TX Park Ranger).

element: Family-to-SOC crosswalk as the only occupational join
rationale: States hire on classes, not SOC. Add a versioned state-class crosswalk layer (minimal_common_fields.csv) alongside SOC and OPM.

State ladders use years plus autonomy and supervision (TX I-V; WA 1-6; MI 9/10/P11/12), and years are substitutable. Crosswalk on supervisory status and autonomy as well as years; years alone mis-map across systems.

element: Sector application text as illustration seeds
rationale: Some Public Agencies notes are usable seeds for state enactment notes (e.g. 4.7.3 'Municipal stormwater utilities, MS4 programs'), but most are generic. Keep with provenance only where a state or local variant is confirmed.
